exothermicity_ladder_same_dft_level.finding: The cage costs 4.60 kcal/mol of abstraction exothermicity relative to the acyclic tertiary site at the SAME level of theory. That is direct quantitative evidence for the pyramidalization prediction: the bridgehead is tertiary by substitution but only 60 percent of the way from primary to acyclic-tertiary in exothermicity. It also reduces the expectation of a submerged barrier here, since submergence at isobutane occurs at -38.38 and this site is 4.60 less exothermic.
exothermicity_ladder_same_dft_level.do_not_extrapolate: A Bell-Evans-Polanyi line through two points tests nothing, and the cage geometry is precisely what such an extrapolation would assume away. No barrier is predicted here.

spurious_agreement_warning.why_this_is_not_agreement: These are DIFFERENT QUANTITIES and the closeness is a coincidence of the category error this lane identified earlier. A 298 K bond dissociation enthalpy is lower than the bare electronic D by the zero-point reduction, roughly 4 kcal/mol for a C-H homolysis, partly offset by about 1 kcal/mol of thermal terms. Applying that correction moves this result to roughly 100 kcal/mol, i.e. BELOW the experimental value rather than on top of it. So the raw comparison flatters the calculation and the corrected one does not. This is a concrete instance of why the electronic-versus-enthalpy mismatch matters: uncorrected, it manufactured an apparent bullseye.
